records.name: Practice Gallery
records.summary: A contemporary art gallery that puts up a new show about once a month, with opening nights open to visitors.
records.what_you_do: See the shows and come to the opening nights, or follow the site's New Member Call link to ask about joining.

schedule.text: New shows about once a month, with opening nights posted on the site (one was a First Friday, 6 to 9 pm)

first_step.how: Go to the next opening listed on the Practice Gallery site and see the show. To ask about membership, use the New Member Call page.
first_step.basis: Shows and openings are open to the public, and the site has a membership call, though its terms are not printed.

records.notes: Address comes from the IRS filing (319 North 11th), not the website, which prints none. The site has no email or phone. One run is listed as June 5 to June 31, 2026, which is not a real date, so it is not used. Post dates such as 10/2/26 look like posting dates and are not counted. painting_drawing is the closest interest tag for a gallery that shows many media.

records.name: The Questers
records.summary: A nonprofit history group with local chapters across the country. Members learn local history, help keep historic places going, and raise money for restoration projects.
records.what_you_do: Join a local chapter to study history, raise restoration money, and share local stories. The Philadelphia headquarters, a historic building, is visited by appointment.

cost.text: Dues are not printed on the site

first_step.how: Call headquarters at 215-923-5183 or email questers210@questers1944.org and ask which chapter meets closest to you.
first_step.basis: Joining is through chapters, but the site prints no dues, application steps or meeting times, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Legal name Questers Inc. The organization is national, with its headquarters in Philadelphia. The site names no Philadelphia chapter and no meeting times. Its dates are historical (1944 founding, 1802 building, 1967 purchase), so status rests on a working site with no dated items. Confirm a chapter that meets in or near Philadelphia before promoting.

records.name: Real Life CDC
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps people get back on their feet after homelessness, incarceration or addiction. It offers life coaching, workshops and help with food, jobs, school and housing.
records.what_you_do: Ask about one-on-one life coaching, leadership and life skills workshops, or help with food, employment, education or housing.

first_step.how: Call 215-792-3298, or send a request through the contact form on reallifecdc.org, and ask which programs are taking people now.
first_step.basis: The way in is a phone call or form, but the site does not describe how enrollment works or whether there is a waitlist.

records.notes: The events calendar showed no events from September 27 to October 31, 2026. The only printed year is a 2018 footer, which is not counted as evidence. Status is probably_active only because the site loads with current service descriptions; no dated item was found. The site lists no email. Audience tags reflect the site's stated focus on people re-entering after homelessness, incarceration or addiction rehabilitation.

records.name: Rebel Ventures
records.summary: A youth-run healthy food business where high school students develop healthy food products, sell them to schools, and work with kids on cooking and hands-on learning.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can offer help in the kitchen or office, and the team says roles can be shaped around what a person can add. High school students can look at job openings, and adults can apply to mentor.

first_step.how: Email rebelventures215@gmail.com with what you can offer, or read the volunteer page at rvcrew.com/volunteer. High school students can check the high school entrepreneur page.
first_step.basis: The site invites volunteers and gives a contact, but sets no sign-up process or start dates.

records.notes: The site names no city or street address and prints no dates. The IRS record lists a Philadelphia P.O. box (19101), which is the only basis for listing it here as Philadelphia. Confirm the service area and kitchen location before promoting. The 1.6 million products sold figure has no date, so it is not used as evidence.

records.name: ReGen250
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit working on regional sustainability. It runs three programs across the six-state Mid-Atlantic region, plus partners abroad.
records.what_you_do: Get updates through the newsletter, follow the announced events and fundraisers, or donate. The site mentions part-time volunteers but describes no sign-up step.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on regen250.org, or call 610-504-2245 and ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site offers a newsletter and a contact page, but no volunteer or event sign-up is described.

records.notes: The home page shows only a 2026 copyright, which is not evidence. No dated events, news or Philadelphia-specific program was found. Most of the work is regional or abroad, so the Philadelphia link rests on the office address. The contact page publishes no organizational email.

records.name: Responsible Preservation Inc
records.notes: The website field held an attorney's name, not a web address. This group was not searched, because the two searches went to groups with a better chance of a public page. Nothing is known about what it does or how to join, so no summary, categories or first step are written. Held back until a public page is found.

records.name: Rittenhop
records.summary: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday afternoon in Rittenhouse Square, with jam sessions, jazz events and a holiday party.
records.what_you_do: Come dance the Sunday swing, or bring a horn to a jam session. The group also runs jazz events and a jazz crawl.

schedule.text: Sundays, 1 to 3:30 pm, rain or shine. Jam sessions and special dates are posted on the site, and weather or venue changes go out on Discord.

locations.label: Rittenhouse Square (usually the southwest corner, by the bench with the goat statue)

cost.text: Free. The site also takes donations to pay live bands.

first_step.how: Go to Rittenhouse Square on a Sunday between 1 and 3:30 pm, look for the bench with the goat statue in the southwest corner, and join in.
first_step.basis: Free and open to anyone who shows up. The site does not say whether lessons or dance experience are needed.

records.notes: The Sep 22, 2026 post refers to a jam session 'that Sunday' at Liberty Garden instead of the square. Posts run through 2026 across all seasons, so year_round is supported. The site prints no email or phone. The Discord link is not recorded because no URL was seen. A dance team named Jazz Attack is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Ruby Housing Inc
records.notes: The IRS record gives the 2042-48 Arch Street office, which is also the headquarters address of Mission First Housing Group, the site named in the batch's website field. Mission First is an affordable housing developer and property manager. Its site never mentions Ruby Housing, and no community program for this entity was found, so it is recorded as a business, not a group. Mission First's own public events are not counted for this entity.

records.name: Scenario Journal
records.notes: An online journal about urban landscape design, run by an independent nonprofit that Penn's Stuart Weitzman School of Design supports. Its public way in is reading, submitting work and donating. No meetings, classes, volunteer or membership programs were found. The newest dated item is Issue 07, printed as Fall 2019 with no month, so status is dormant. The 2026 copyright footer is not counted.

records.name: ScoopUSA Media Community Education Program
records.notes: ScoopUSA Media is a print and digital newspaper. Its community education program page describes planned forums and monthly meetings but prints no dates, places, prices or sign-up step. The only dated item is a heading for a 2022 launch event, so status is dormant. No public way in was found, so it is hidden until one appears.

records.name: Seger Park Dog Owners Association
records.summary: Volunteers who look after the off-leash dog park in Seger Park. They run the dog run, organize neighborhood cleanups, and host community events with local businesses and musicians.
records.what_you_do: Dog owners use the park and can join as members. Volunteers can help with cleanups and events by emailing the president.

cost.text: The membership page exists, but dues are not printed on the home page

first_step.how: Read the park rules on segerdogpark.org, then use the Become a Member link. To volunteer, email president.spdoa@gmail.com.
first_step.basis: Anyone who follows the park rules can use the park, and the site links a membership page and a volunteer email, though no dues are printed.

records.notes: Found by searching the group name, which surfaced segerdogpark.org; the group's own site is the source for every fact here. The site prints no event dates; the Woofstock concert series is only described as 'this summer'. A third-party listing gives 1020 Lombard St, which disagrees with the site's 1001 Rodman St, so the record uses the site. The batch website field said 'Seger Park Advisory Council', a separate body listed in leads_only. The 2019 copyright footer is not counted.

records.name: Seger Park Tennis Club
records.summary: A tennis club for Seger Park that has paused its activities because the park's court reservation system is suspended.
records.notes: Do not present as joinable now. The suspension notice is undated. The site has no dates, prices, contacts or street address, so no audience, schedule or first step is recorded. Hold this record back until the club confirms it is running again. The IRS address (1218 Walnut St) is not verified as a court location, so no location is listed.

records.name: SEPTA Youth Advisory Council
records.summary: A nonprofit of young transit riders in Southeastern Pennsylvania. Members give feedback to SEPTA, educate riders, and push for student transit passes on campuses.
records.what_you_do: Apply online to join. Members give SEPTA input, table on college campuses, track transit laws and run trainings, such as a UPass training.

first_step.how: Create an account on septayac.org, then complete the application on the Apply page. Questions go to contact@septayac.org.
first_step.basis: Members apply online, and selection runs on a rolling basis with earlier applicants first, so the way in needs an application.

records.notes: Age range is 18 to 25; the schema holds only the minimum. The events page lists a UPass Training on September 26, 1 to 3 pm, with no year printed, so it is not counted as dated evidence. Time commitment, dues and pay are not stated. Residence rules are not stated. Founded 2009 per the site.

records.name: Skilladelphia
records.summary: Basketball and lacrosse training for girls and nonbinary kids ages 5 to 14, with skills clinics, after-school care and summer camps. Coaches and guest speakers are paid.
records.what_you_do: Kids join skills clinics, aftercare and summer camps. Families can register for fall programs, and the group also holds a fundraiser and a 3-on-3 tournament.

cost.text: Described as low or no cost. Prices are not printed on the site.

first_step.how: Email mac@skilladelphia.org or use the Register for Fall Programs link on skilladelphia.org to ask about the next clinic or camp, with dates and prices.
first_step.basis: Families can register through the site or by email, but no prices or dates are printed, so the first step is a question.

records.notes: Two domains: skilladelphia.org (current) and skilladelphiabasketballacademy.org, which says its site has changed. Ages print as 5 to 14 on the current site and 6 to 14 on the older one; the record uses 5. The current site's email link points to a different domain, so confirm the address before sharing. Event dates: Baskets and Bubbles on October 3 and a 3-on-3 Tournament on September 26, neither with a year. Summer Camp 2026 is the only year printed, so no last_sign_of_life is set. Lacrosse has no interest tag; the record uses basketball. No street address is printed; the IRS record lists 766 S 7th St, not verified on the site. Partner Old Pine Community Center is in leads_only.

records.name: Slavaart
records.notes: The website field held 'PHP', not a web address. One search for the name found no page about this group. Nothing is known about what it does or how to join, so no summary, categories or first step are written. Held back until a public page is found. The IRS address on file is not verified.

leads_only.name: Old Pine Community Center
leads_only.note: Named on Skilladelphia's site as its partner and as host of a 3-on-3 event; no own website identified, not checked

notes: Searches: 2 of 2 used. Fetches: 23 used of 60. Verdicts: publish 12, not_a_group 2, hide 1. Three batch websites were not web addresses: Responsible Preservation (an attorney's name), Seger Park Dog Owners ('Seger Park Advisory Council') and Slavaart ('PHP'). Responsible Preservation was not searched, so it is held as publish with unknown status and no source. Slavaart: one search found no page, so it is held the same way. Seger Park Dog Owners: the search surfaced segerdogpark.org, which is the group's own site and was read. Seger Park Tennis Club is publish, but its site says operations are suspended; recommend holding it back. Two records (Responsible Preservation, Slavaart) lack summary and source and will not go live. Dated items come from group-owned pages only. One guessed domain (mission1st.org) returned an empty page; the batch domain was used instead. No pages were blocked and no rate limiting occurred. Leads: the three leads_only items have no own URL recorded, so they were not fetched; Old Pine Community Center's own website should be found on the next pass.
